body: Every query is cached under its queryKey. Official guidance is to use an array key, often with a scope string first and then the variables that change the result (['todos', { status, page }]). When a key changes, React Query treats it as a different query. Matching keys is also how you invalidate or prefetch: invalidate queries that start with ['todos'] after a mutation. Keep keys serializable and include every input the queryFn depends on. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: useMutation runs writes and can invalidate related queries
body: useMutation({ mutationFn, onSuccess }) is the hook for creates, updates, and deletes. Call mutate(variables) or mutateAsync(variables). Unlike useQuery, mutations are not automatically retried in the same way and are not cached as a query. In onSuccess (or the mutation cache callbacks) call queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['todos'] }) so lists refetch. The hook exposes isPending, error, and data for UI state. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: npm init playwright@latest scaffolds Playwright Test and browsers
body: Install with npm init playwright@latest (or yarn create playwright / pnpm create playwright). The wizard picks TypeScript or JavaScript, a tests folder, an optional GitHub Actions workflow, and whether to install browser binaries. Run tests with npx playwright test (add --headed, --project=chromium, a file path, or --ui). Open the HTML report with npx playwright show-report. Update later with npm install -D @playwright/test@latest and npx playwright install --with-deps. Node.js latest 22.x, 24.x, or 26.x is required. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Tests import test and expect from @playwright/test and use the page fixture
body: import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test'; test('has title', async ({ page }) => { await page.goto('https://playwright.dev/'); await expect(page).toHaveTitle(/Playwright/); }). The page fixture is an isolated browser page. Playwright waits for actionability before clicks and for assertions to pass, so you usually do not add manual sleeps. Tests in one file run with that same test() API; configure browsers and retries in playwright.config.ts. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: getByRole and other locators auto-wait before actions
body: Locate elements with the Locators API, most often page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Get started' }), then chain .click(), .fill(), .check(), .press(), or .selectOption(). Playwright waits until the element is actionable before performing the action, which removes many race conditions. Prefer role, label, and text locators over CSS or XPath when you can, because they follow how users and assistive tech see the page. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Async expect matchers wait until the condition is true
body: Playwright assertions are designed to retry until they pass or time out. Use await expect(page).toHaveTitle(/Playwright/), await expect(locator).toBeVisible(), toContainText(), toHaveText(), toHaveURL(), toBeChecked(), and similar matchers. Generic matchers such as toEqual or toBeTruthy are synchronous and do not take await — use them only on values you already have. This auto-waiting is what makes tests less flaky than assert-immediately libraries. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Each test gets an isolated BrowserContext; hooks wrap setup
body: The built-in page fixture belongs to a fresh Browser Context, equivalent to a new browser profile, so tests do not share cookies, storage, or pages even when they run in the same browser. Group tests with test.describe and use test.beforeEach / test.afterEach for per-test setup, or test.beforeAll / test.afterAll once per worker. A typical beforeEach is await page.goto(startUrl) so each test starts from a known page. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: npx sv create scaffolds a SvelteKit app in src/routes
body: The easiest way to start is npx sv create my-app, then cd my-app and npm run dev (install dependencies first if the scaffolder did not). The dev server defaults to http://localhost:5173. Each page is a Svelte component, and you add pages as files under src/routes. The first visit is server-rendered, then the client-side app takes over. The CLI can set up TypeScript and other tooling during create. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: +page, +layout, +error, and +server files define routes
body: Routes live in src/routes. +page.svelte is the page UI; +page.js or +page.server.js load data for that page. +layout.svelte (and +layout.js / +layout.server.js) wraps child routes. +error.svelte renders errors. +server.js (or .ts) defines HTTP handlers for that path. Folders name the URL segment; dynamic parameters use [param] folders. Colocate components used by only one route next to these files. $types is generated for each route's typings. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: load functions in +page.js or +page.server.js provide page data
body: Export a load function from +page.js (universal) or +page.server.js (server-only) to supply data for a route. Server load can use secrets, cookies, and headers; universal load can also run in the browser. Return an object that becomes data in the page component. Use the provided fetch so requests are tracked correctly during SSR. Layout load functions contribute data to child pages. Redirect or throw errors from load when the user should not see the page. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Form actions in +page.server.js handle POST submissions
body: Export const actions from +page.server.js. The default action runs when a <form method='POST'> on that page is submitted. Named actions (for example login and register) are invoked with action='?/register' or a button formaction='?/register'. Actions always use POST because GET must not have side effects. You can post to another page's action with action='/login'. use:enhance progressively enhances the form so the page can stay put and apply the result without a full reload. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: authjs.dev documents Auth.js / next-auth v5, which is still published as a beta
body: Auth.js is the documentation brand for next-auth@5.0.0-beta and later and for packages under the @auth/* namespace. Official getting-started docs state that they cover next-auth@5.0.0-beta and later; v4 docs remain at next-auth.js.org. On npm, the latest tag for next-auth may still be v4, so follow the Auth.js install instructions (including a beta tag when the docs say to use one) rather than assuming npm install next-auth installs v5. The library is runtime-agnostic and built on Web APIs. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: AUTH_SECRET is required; generate it with npx auth secret
body: The only mandatory environment variable is AUTH_SECRET, a random value used to encrypt tokens and email verification hashes. Generate and write it with the official CLI: npx auth secret, which also appends it to the framework's env file (for example .env.local in Next.js). Do not commit the secret or put it in client-side code. You do not need to install @auth/core yourself; framework packages depend on it and official docs say users should not interact with it directly. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: auth.ts exports handlers, signIn, signOut, and auth from NextAuth()
body: The recommended Next.js setup is a root auth.ts: import NextAuth from 'next-auth' and export const { handlers, signIn, signOut, auth } = NextAuth({ providers: [] }). Then create the App Router route handler at app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts that re-exports GET and POST from handlers. Fill the providers array with built-in providers imported from next-auth/providers/*. Other frameworks have their own init helpers but share this auth.ts convention. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Next.js 16 renamed middleware.ts to proxy.ts for the auth wrapper
body: Auth.js can wrap a Next.js proxy (formerly middleware) so the session is kept alive as requests pass through. Official installation notes that as of Next.js 16, middleware.ts has been renamed to proxy.ts. On Next.js 16, use the proxy file with the auth wrapper; on older Next.js, keep middleware.ts and export { auth as middleware }. This optional step is for session refresh and protecting routes, not a substitute for the /api/auth route handler. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Auth.js supports OAuth, magic links, credentials, and WebAuthn
body: Official getting-started lists four authentication methods: OAuth (Google, GitHub, LinkedIn, and many others), magic links (email providers such as Resend, Nodemailer, or SendGrid), credentials (username/password or an external API), and WebAuthn/passkeys. Optional database adapters persist users and accounts if you need them. Configure each method as a provider in the NextAuth({ providers }) array (or the equivalent for your framework) rather than rolling a custom token endpoint. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Install the Bun executable with the official script or a package manager
body: Bun ships as a single executable. On macOS and Linux: curl -fsSL https://bun.com/install | bash (Linux needs unzip; kernel 5.6+ is recommended). On Windows 10 1809 or later: powershell -c "irm bun.sh/install.ps1|iex". You can also npm install -g bun, brew install oven-sh/bun/bun, scoop install bun, or docker pull oven/bun. Verify with bun --version and bun --revision. If the shell says command not found, add ~/.bun/bin to PATH (BUN_INSTALL=$HOME/.bun). This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: bun run executes TypeScript and package.json scripts directly
body: bun run index.ts runs a TypeScript or JavaScript file without a separate transpile step. Scripts in package.json work as bun run start (or bun run <script>). Official quickstart notes that bun run has much less overhead than npm run. bun install installs packages; bun add adds one. A typical new project uses { "module": "index.ts", "type": "module" } and may include @types/bun. bun init can scaffold that layout. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Bun.serve starts an HTTP server with a routes object
body: const server = Bun.serve({ port: 3000, routes: { '/': indexHtml, '/figlet': () => new Response(body) } }) is the documented pattern. Route values can be a Response, an HTML import, or a function that returns a Response. After start, server.url is the listening origin (for example http://localhost:3000/). This is the built-in server; you do not need Express to serve HTTP from Bun. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: bun:test is a Jest-compatible runner invoked with bun test
body: import { expect, test, describe } from 'bun:test' and write test('2 + 2', () => { expect(2 + 2).toBe(4) }). Group suites with describe, and use async test callbacks or a done callback (you must call done() or the test hangs). A third argument to test() is a timeout in milliseconds (default 5000). Run the runner with bun test. Long term, Bun aims for complete Jest compatibility; module mocks, hooks, and snapshots are documented separately. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: create_engine() is the starting point for every application
body: from sqlalchemy import create_engine; engine = create_engine('sqlite+pysqlite:///:memory:', echo=True) builds an Engine. The URL names the dialect (sqlite), the DBAPI (pysqlite, optional when there is a default), and the location (/:memory: here). echo=True logs SQL, which is useful while learning. The Engine is usually a single global per database and includes a connection pool. create_engine() does not connect immediately; the first real operation opens a connection (lazy initialization). This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: SQLAlchemy 2.1 is one Unified Tutorial covering Core and ORM
body: SQLAlchemy has two APIs: Core (engine, Connection, Result, SQL expression language, metadata) and the ORM (mapped classes, Session, relationship()), which builds on Core. In 2.0-style (including 2.1) the ORM uses the same select() construct as Core, and transactional patterns line up between Connection and Session. Official 2.1 docs ask you to confirm sqlalchemy.__version__ starts with 2.1. New code should follow the Unified Tutorial, not the 1.x Query API. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: DeclarativeBase and mapped_column define ORM mapped classes
body: In the 2.x ORM, subclass DeclarativeBase for your Base, then declare classes with __tablename__ and typed attributes: id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True). Import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, and mapped_column from sqlalchemy.orm. Call Base.metadata.create_all(engine) to emit CREATE TABLE in simple scripts, or use Alembic for real migrations. This declarative form is the documented quickstart style in 2.1. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Session and select() are the 2.x way to load and persist objects
body: Open a session with with Session(engine) as session: (or a sessionmaker factory). Add new objects with session.add(), then session.commit() to persist. Load rows with select(User) and session.scalars(...) or session.execute(...). Filter with select(User).where(User.name == 'ed'). Do not use the legacy Query API in new 2.1 code. Close or context-manage the Session so connections return to the pool. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: FunctionAgent runs an LLM with Python callables as tools
body: The official starter builds an agent with FunctionAgent from llama_index.core.agent.workflow, passing tools=[multiply], an llm such as OpenAI(model='gpt-4o-mini'), and a system_prompt. Call await agent.run('What is 1234 * 4567?') inside asyncio.run(main()). Tool functions and their docstrings become the tool schema. Official docs recommend async code because many model providers support async calls. Default LLM wiring uses OpenAI; set OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Pass a Context to FunctionAgent.run to keep chat history
body: AgentWorkflow (including FunctionAgent) can remember prior turns when you pass a Context. Create ctx = Context(agent) from llama_index.core.workflow, then await agent.run('My name is Logan', ctx=ctx) and later await agent.run('What is my name?', ctx=ctx). Without a shared Context, each run is independent. Keep one Context per conversation, not a global shared across users. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: VectorStoreIndex and SimpleDirectoryReader add RAG to an agent
body: documents = SimpleDirectoryReader('data').load_data(); index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(documents); query_engine = index.as_query_engine() builds an in-memory index over files in data/. Wrap query_engine.aquery(query) in an async tool and pass that tool to FunctionAgent so the agent can search documents. With no Settings.embed_model configured, VectorStoreIndex falls back to OpenAIEmbedding (historically text-embedding-ada-002). Official docs recommend passing OpenAIEmbedding(model='text-embedding-3-small') explicitly in new projects, or a local HuggingFaceEmbedding. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: storage_context.persist saves an index so you can reload it
body: index.storage_context.persist('storage') writes the index to disk. Later: from llama_index.core import StorageContext, load_index_from_storage; storage_context = StorageContext.from_defaults(persist_dir='storage'); index = load_index_from_storage(storage_context). If you used a vector store integration other than the default, you can often rebuild with VectorStoreIndex.from_vector_store(vector_store) instead of the local persist folder. Persisting avoids re-embedding documents on every process start. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: React Router 8 has Declarative, Data, and Framework modes
body: React Router is a multi-strategy router. Declarative mode is the basic <BrowserRouter> style with Route, Link, useNavigate, and useLocation. Data mode moves route config outside of render and adds loader, action, and useFetcher via createBrowserRouter and RouterProvider. Framework mode wraps Data mode with a Vite plugin for type-safe route modules, href, code splitting, and SPA/SSR/static strategies. Features are additive: moving Declarative → Data → Framework adds capabilities and reduces some architectural control. Official docs say upgrading from v7 is generally non-breaking if you are caught up on future flags. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Declarative mode wraps the app in BrowserRouter
body: import { BrowserRouter } from 'react-router' and render <BrowserRouter><App /></BrowserRouter> (from react-dom). This mode gives URL matching, navigation, and active states with APIs such as Link, useNavigate, and useLocation. Official advice is to use it when you want the simplest router, you are coming from earlier React Router versions and are happy with BrowserRouter, or you already have your own data layer. Import from 'react-router', not the old 'react-router-dom' package name, in current v8 docs. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: createBrowserRouter and RouterProvider enable loaders and actions
body: import { createBrowserRouter, RouterProvider } from 'react-router'. let router = createBrowserRouter([{ path: '/', Component: Root, loader: loadRootData }]); then render <RouterProvider router={router} />. Because the route tree is defined outside of React render, loaders, actions, pending states, and useFetcher are available. Official docs recommend Data mode when you want those features but still want to control bundling and the server yourself, including apps that started a data router in v6.4. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Framework mode uses a route module API and create-react-router
body: Framework mode is scaffolded with the official installer (npx create-react-router@latest) and a routes file that uses index() and route() from @react-router/dev/routes, for example route('products/:pid', './product.tsx'). Route modules can export loader and a default component; types come from './+types/product.tsx' (Route.LoaderArgs, Route.ComponentProps, loaderData, typed params). You also get type-safe href, code splitting, and SPA, SSR, or static rendering. Official docs point newcomers who just want to build with React (or who are comparing Next.js, SvelteKit, and similar) to Framework mode. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Install Vitest 5 and run tests once with vitest run
body: Install as a dev dependency: npm install -D vitest. Yarn users must also add vite (yarn add -D vitest vite) because vite is now a required peer dependency of vitest. Vitest 5 requires Vite >= 6.4.0 and Node.js >= 22.12.0. Test files must contain .test. or .spec. in the name: import { expect, test } from 'vitest'; test('adds 1 + 2 to equal 3', () => { expect(sum(1, 2)).toBe(3) }). Add "test": "vitest" to package.json scripts; plain vitest watches for changes, while vitest run runs once and exits. Vitest reads vite.config.* by default, or a dedicated vitest.config.* exporting defineConfig({ test: { ... } }) from 'vitest/config'. Generated reports and artifacts go in a .vitest/ directory, which the docs recommend adding to .gitignore. With Bun as the package manager, run bun run test, not bun test (that starts Bun's own test runner). This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Vitest 5 behavior changes: clearMocks on by default, unawaited assertions fail, vi.mock must be top level
body: Vitest 5.0 changes defaults that can break v4-era tests. clearMocks now defaults to true: vi.clearAllMocks() runs before every test, so mock call history recorded in setup files, at module top level, or in beforeAll is cleared before the test asserts (implementations are kept); set test: { clearMocks: false } to restore v4 behavior. Async assertions such as expect(p).resolves, .rejects, and toMatchFileSnapshot now fail the test when not awaited (v4 auto-awaited with a warning), so write await expect(p).resolves.toBe(1). vi.mock, vi.unmock, and vi.hoisted inside a function, block, or describe/test callback now throw; move them to module top level (vi.doMock and vi.doUnmock may still be called anywhere). expect.poll rejects if the callback or assertion does not settle within timeout, and the callback receives an AbortSignal. testNamePattern (-t) matches the full name joined with ' > ', e.g. vitest -t 'math > adds'. Inline test.projects now inherit the root config (extends defaults to true), including plugins and resolve.alias; set extends: false to opt out. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Vitest 5 removed APIs: bench is a test fixture, test.sequential is gone, old entry points removed
body: bench is no longer a top-level import from 'vitest'; destructure it from the test context: test('sort', async ({ bench }) => { await bench('sort', () => { [3, 1, 2].sort() }).run() }). bench.skip/only/todo, benchmark.reporters, benchmark.outputFile, benchmark.compare (--compare), and benchmark.outputJson (--outputJson) are removed; use test.skip/only/todo on the surrounding test, top-level test.reporters, and --reporter=json --outputFile=<file>. test.sequential, describe.sequential, and the sequential option are removed: use test('x', { concurrent: false }, fn) or describe('s', { concurrent: false }, fn). Entry points deprecated in 4.1 are gone: import from vitest/node instead of vitest/coverage or vitest/reporters, from vitest/runtime instead of vitest/environments or vitest/snapshot, and use TestRunner from 'vitest' instead of vitest/runners or vitest/suite (e.g. TestRunner.getCurrentTest()). vitest no longer depends on @vitest/expect; use expect, expect.extend, and chai from 'vitest'. Custom matcher types augment Matchers<R, T>; the global jest.Matchers interface is no longer read. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Install pytest 9 in a virtual environment and write a first assert test
body: Install into a virtual environment, not the system Python: python3 -m venv .venv, source .venv/bin/activate, pip install -U pytest. In a uv project (pyproject.toml) run uv add --dev pytest and prefix commands with uv run, e.g. uv run pytest. pytest --version should print pytest 9.2.0; pytest 9 requires Python >= 3.10 (3.9 support was dropped in 9.0). Tests are plain functions using bare assert statements: def test_answer(): assert func(3) == 5. Assertion introspection reports intermediate values (assert 4 == 5, where 4 = func(3)), so no assertEqual-style helpers are needed. Running pytest with no arguments collects files named test_*.py or *_test.py in the current directory and its subdirectories. Check exceptions with import pytest, then with pytest.raises(SystemExit): f(). Use pytest -q for quiet output. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: pytest 9 native TOML config: [tool.pytest] or pytest.toml, plus strict = true
body: Since pytest 9.0, pyproject.toml supports native TOML types under [tool.pytest]: minversion = "9.0", addopts = ["-ra", "-q"], testpaths = ["tests", "integration"] (real TOML arrays, not space-separated strings). The older [tool.pytest.ini_options] table (INI compatibility mode, every value a string or list of strings, e.g. addopts = "-ra -q") still works, but the two tables cannot be used at the same time. A standalone pytest.toml or hidden .pytest.toml uses a [pytest] table and takes precedence over all other config files, even when empty; pytest.ini / .pytest.ini come next. pytest 9 warns when configuration is spread over more than one file, because only one is used. Strict mode (added in 9.0): strict = true enables strict_config, strict_markers, strict_parametrization_ids, and strict_xfail at once, and will also turn on strictness options added in future releases, so the docs advise it only with a pinned or locked pytest version. Individual options can still be overridden, e.g. strict = true with strict_parametrization_ids = false. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Upgrading to pytest 9.x: built-in subtests, removed-in-9 errors, keyword-only parametrize arguments
body: 9.0: subtests are built in (formerly the pytest-subtests plugin): def test_files(subtests: pytest.Subtests): for p in paths: with subtests.test(path=str(p)): assert check(p). Each failure is reported separately; unittest TestCase.subTest() also works. PytestRemovedIn9Warning became an error, and those features are gone as of 9.1. Overlapping or duplicate path arguments collapse (pytest a/ a/b runs a/ once, pytest x.py x.py runs once); --keep-duplicates restores the old behavior. CI mode now needs $CI or $BUILD_NUMBER set to a non-empty value. 9.1 deprecates non-Collection iterables such as generators as parametrize argvalues (pass a list or tuple), class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods (use @classmethod), and --pastebin (now the pytest-pastebin plugin). 9.2 (2026-10-27): indirect, ids, and scope of @pytest.mark.parametrize are keyword-only, e.g. parametrize('x', [1, 2], ids=['a', 'b']); -c with a missing, directory, or unloadable path is a usage error; a plugin that cannot be found exits with code 4 (USAGE_ERROR) and one that fails to import exits with 3 (INTERNAL_ERROR); non-string values for string options in [tool.pytest.ini_options] emit PytestRemovedIn10Warning; yield_fixture is scheduled for removal. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: uv 0.13 project workflow: uv init, uv add, uv lock, uv run, uv sync
body: uv init hello-world (or uv init inside an existing directory) creates pyproject.toml, .python-version, README.md, .gitignore, a git repo, and a packaged src layout: src/hello_world/__init__.py, a [project.scripts] entry hello-world = "hello_world:main", and [build-system] requires = ["uv_build>=0.13.9,<0.14"], build-backend = "uv_build". Run it with uv run hello-world. The first uv run, uv sync, or uv lock creates .venv and uv.lock; uv.lock is a cross-platform TOML lockfile that should be committed and never edited by hand. uv add requests (or uv add 'requests==2.31.0', uv add git+https://github.com/psf/requests) updates pyproject.toml, the lockfile, and the environment; uv add -r requirements.txt -c constraints.txt migrates a requirements file; uv remove requests removes one; uv lock --upgrade-package requests upgrades a single package and keeps the rest of the lock. Before every uv run, uv checks that the lock matches pyproject.toml and the environment matches the lock: uv run -- flask run -p 3000 or uv run example.py. Alternatively uv sync, then source .venv/bin/activate (Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate). uv run does not remove extraneous packages by default. uv build writes an sdist and wheel to dist/; uv version --short prints the project version. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Run Python scripts with uv: --with, PEP 723 inline dependencies, uv add --script, shebang, script lockfiles
body: uv run example.py runs a script; in a directory with pyproject.toml it installs the current project first, so pass --no-project before the script name (uv run --no-project example.py) when the script does not need the project. One-off dependencies: uv run --with rich example.py, or uv run --with 'rich>12,<13' example.py (repeat --with for more). Prefer inline metadata (PEP 723): uv init --script example.py --python 3.12 creates it, and uv add --script example.py 'requests<3' rich writes a header block: # /// script, # requires-python = ">=3.12", # dependencies = ["requests<3", "rich"], # ///. The dependencies field is required even if empty. With inline metadata, project dependencies are ignored (no --no-project needed) and uv downloads the required Python if missing. Executable scripts: first line #!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script, then chmod +x. Lock a script explicitly with uv lock --script example.py (writes example.py.lock beside it, reused by uv run --script, uv add --script, uv export --script, uv tree --script). For reproducibility add [tool.uv] exclude-newer = "2023-10-16T00:00:00Z" (RFC 3339) inside the metadata block. Alternate index: uv add --index "https://example.com/simple" --script example.py pkg. Pick an interpreter per run with uv run --python 3.10 example.py; read from stdin with uv run -. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Upgrading to uv 0.12/0.13: packaged uv init, Python 3.15 default, stable-first pre-releases, stricter hashes
body: 0.12.0 (2026-07-28): uv init now defines a uv_build build system, puts code in src/<name>, and adds a [project.scripts] command (uv run <name>); use uv init --no-package for the old main.py layout without a build system. Pre-release default is if-necessary: stable versions first, falling back to pre-releases, including ones required transitively (--prerelease disallow opts out; if-necessary-or-explicit is a deprecated alias). uv run path/to/script.py now discovers the project from the script's directory (opt out with --project .). uv venv --clear refuses a non-venv directory unless --force. uv init --project is an error (use uv init <path> or --directory). --require-hashes inside requirements.txt is enforced, MD5-only hashes are rejected in hash-checking mode, and .tar.bz2/.tar.xz sdists are rejected. 0.13.0 (2026-10-09): Python 3.15 is the default stable version for downloads when none is requested or pinned (uv python pin 3.14 or --python 3.14 to stay); --require-hashes in -c constraints files is honored; editable (-e) entries in constraints files are errors; --constraint/--override/--exclude/--build-constraint values are single paths (repeat the flag instead of quoting a space-separated list). Cache entries changed, so uv may re-download or rebuild after upgrading. Bump any uv_build upper bound, e.g. uv_build>=0.13.0,<0.14. Latest patch: 0.13.9 (2026-11-17). This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Ruff 0.17 quick start: uv add --dev ruff, ruff check --fix, ruff format, config, pre-commit
body: Add Ruff to a uv project with uv add --dev ruff (or pip install ruff), then run uv run ruff check (lint) and uv run ruff format (format, default 88-character line length); both run on the current directory unless you pass paths. Apply safe fixes with ruff check --fix; unsafe fixes need --fix --unsafe-fixes or unsafe-fixes = true. Ruff reads the first pyproject.toml, ruff.toml, or .ruff.toml in the file's directory or a parent. pyproject.toml: [tool.ruff] line-length = 79, then [tool.ruff.lint] extend-select = ["UP", "D"] and [tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle] convention = "google"; in ruff.toml drop the tool.ruff prefix ([lint], [lint.pydocstyle]). Prefer extend-select over select so the default rule set (F, E, B, UP, RUF and more, minus formatter-overlapping style rules) stays on. The Python version comes from [project] requires-python = ">=3.10" or target-version = "py310". pre-commit: repo https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit, rev: v0.17.6, hooks ruff-check then ruff-format (add types_or: [python, pyi, jupyter, markdown] to ruff-format for Markdown). When adopting a rule on legacy code, ruff check --select UP035 --add-noqa . (or --add-ignore) adds suppressions to existing violations. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Ruff suppression comments: noqa, ruff: ignore[...], ruff: disable/enable ranges, file-ignore, RUF100
body: Line level: x = 1  # noqa: F841 (several codes: # noqa: E741, F841; bare # noqa ignores everything). Since 0.16 you can also write # ruff: ignore[F401] at the end of a line, or on its own line above a statement, where it covers the whole logical line (an entire multi-line def signature or list literal); placed inside a multi-line statement it covers only that physical line. Stacked ignore comments all apply to the next logical line. Since 0.15, block ranges: # ruff: disable[E501] ... # ruff: enable[E501]; codes, order, and indentation must match, at least one code is required (no blanket form), and ranges only suppress rules already selected. A disable without a matching enable runs until a less-indented scope and is reported as RUF104, so prefer explicit enable comments. File level: # ruff: noqa, # ruff: noqa: F841 (own line; # flake8: noqa is honored), or # ruff: file-ignore[F401, ARG001] at module scope near the top. For multi-line strings put # noqa after the closing quotes; for import sorting put # noqa: I001 on the first import of the block. Per-path ignores: lint.per-file-ignores. Find and remove stale suppressions with ruff check --extend-select RUF100 --fix; add suppressions for existing violations with --add-noqa or --add-ignore. In preview mode rule names such as unused-import can replace codes. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.

title: Upgrading to Ruff 0.15-0.17: 2026 style, 413 default rules, Markdown formatting, Python 3.11 default, ruff-lsp removed
body: 0.15.0 (2026-02-03): the formatter applies the 2026 style guide (expect a one-time reformat); block suppressions # ruff: disable[CODE] / # ruff: enable[CODE]; extended config files are resolved before Ruff falls back to a default Python version. 0.16.0 (2026-07-23): the default rule set grows from 59 to 413 rules (see the Default Rules page), and 18 opinionated E/F rules leave it (E401, E402, E701-E703, E711-E714, E721, E731, E741-E743, F403, F405, F406, F722); ruff format now formats Python code blocks in Markdown files by default (opt out with extend-exclude = ["*.md"]; skip blocks with <!-- fmt:off --> / <!-- fmt:on -->); # ruff: ignore[CODE] comments work like noqa; check and format --check show fix diffs, and format --check accepts --output-format github or gitlab; JSON output location fields may be null. 0.17.0 (2026-10-09): the default target is Python 3.11 (was 3.10) when neither target-version nor requires-python is set; DTZ001/005/006/007/011/012/901 are no longer default while F406 is; the full output always displays unsafe fixes (applying them still needs --unsafe-fixes); ICN001 expects import datetime as dt; ruff-lsp support is removed (the VS Code extension always uses the native server; ruff.nativeServer is ignored); conda-forge builds drop Python, so python -m ruff and import ruff fail there. Latest patch: 0.17.6 (2026-11-19). This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official documentation.
